title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.35: Matrix Spencer

problems.sourceStatement: Given matrices $A_1,...,A_n \in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfying $||A_i||_{op} \le 1$ where $||.||_{op}$ is the operator norm of matrices. Do there exists signs $\epsilon_1,...,\epsilon_n\in\{-1,1\}$ s.t. $||\sum_{i=1}^n\epsilon_i A_i || =O(\sqrt{n})$.
problems.problem: Prove (or disprove) the Matrix Spencer conjecture: for any $n$ symmetric $d \times d$ matrices of operator norm at most 1, there exist signs $\epsilon_i \in \{-1, 1\}$ such that the operator norm of the signed sum is $O(\sqrt{n})$ (for $d = n$; more generally $O(\sqrt{n \max(1, \log(d/n))})$).
problems.wordDescription: The Matrix Spencer conjecture (due to Zouzias 2012, popularized by Meka 2014) is the matrix analogue of Spencer's 'six standard deviations suffice' theorem: it asks whether signing $n$ unit-norm matrices can balance their sum in operator norm to $O(\sqrt{n})$, the bound that Spencer's theorem gives when all matrices commute (in which case the problem reduces to its diagonal / vector form). Random signings achieve only $O(\sqrt{n \log d})$ by the non-commutative Khintchine inequality / matrix Chernoff bound, and the conjecture says the $\sqrt{\log d}$ factor can be removed. The conjecture remains open in general; notable partial results include rank-$O(\sqrt{n})$ matrices (Hopkins-Raghavendra-Shetty), block-diagonal matrices (Levy-Ramadas-Rothvoss; Dadush-Jiang-Reis), and matrices of rank at most $n/\log^3 n$ (Bansal-Jiang-Meka). Connections to quantum random access codes, Kadison-Singer-type problems, and graph sparsification are known.
problems.mathematicalConditions: There is an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for all $n, d \geq 1$ and all symmetric $d \times d$ matrices $A_1, \dots, A_n$ with $\|A_i\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq 1$, there exist signs $\epsilon \in \{-1, 1\}^n$ with $\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i A_i\right\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C\sqrt{n \max(1, \log(d/n))}$. In the case $d = n$ (as stated on the AimPL page), the claim is $O(\sqrt{n})$.

literature.title: M. Zouzias (2012) — first appearance of the Matrix Spencer conjecture (as cited in R. van Handel, Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024, arXiv:2504.20539)
literature.description: The conjecture is attributed to Zouzias (2012); see also R. Meka, 'Discrepancy: the vector and matrix versions', Windows on Theory blog (2014), which popularized it.

literature.title: R. Meka, Discrepancy: the vector and matrix versions, Windows on Theory blog post, 2014
literature.description: Blog post (2014) that brought the Matrix Spencer conjecture to wide attention; cited as [Mek14] in the literature.

literature.title: R. van Handel (ed.), Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024, arXiv:2504.20539
literature.description: Discusses the Matrix Spencer conjecture in depth, including the commutative and free extremes, and the 'Group Spencer' conjecture of Bandeira-Kunisky-Mixon-Zeng.

literature.title: S. B. Hopkins, P. Raghavendra, A. Shetty, Matrix discrepancy from quantum communication, FOCS 2022
literature.description: Proves the Matrix Spencer conjecture for matrices of rank $O(\sqrt{n})$, via a connection to quantum information theory.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, R. Meka, Resolving Matrix Spencer conjecture up to poly-logarithmic rank, arXiv:2208.11286, 2022
literature.description: Proves the conjecture for matrices with $\|A_i\|_F^2 \leq n/\log^3 n$ (in particular rank at most $n/\log^3 n$), with an efficient algorithm, using improved non-commutative Khintchine inequalities of Bandeira-Boedihardjo-van Handel.

literature.title: D. Dadush, H. Jiang, V. Reis, A new framework for matrix discrepancy: integrality gap bounds for the Lovász Cap Set problem, 2022; A. Levy, H. Ramadas, T. Rothvoss, Deterministic discrepancy minimization via the multiplicative weight update method, 2017
literature.description: Prove the conjecture for block-diagonal matrices (block size $h = O(n/d)$), the DJR paper via covering estimates for relative entropy.

problems.verificationNotes: Verified on 2026-08-25. The conjecture is confirmed to be a recognized open problem attributed to Zouzias (2012) and Meka (2014), with the exact statement $\mathrm{disc}(A_1,\dots,A_n) \leq C\sqrt{n\max(1,\log(d/n))}$ as in arXiv:2410.17887 and arXiv:2208.11286. Matrix Chernoff / non-commutative Khintchine gives $O(\sqrt{n\log d})$, matching the page's '$O(\sqrt{n\log n})$' for $d = n$. Partial results verified: HRS 2022 (rank $O(\sqrt{n})$), LRR 2017 and DJR 2022 (block-diagonal), BJM 2022/2023 (rank $\leq n/\log^3 n$, arXiv:2208.11286). The full conjecture remains open as of 2026.
problems.statusDetails: We can assume that the matrices are symmetric. Matrix Chernoff gives a bound of $O(\sqrt{n\log n})$. The conjecture itself remains open; partial progress: rank $O(\sqrt{n})$ (Hopkins-Raghavendra-Shetty 2022), block-diagonal matrices (Levy-Ramadas-Rothvoss 2017; Dadush-Jiang-Reis 2022), rank at most $n/\log^3 n$ (Bansal-Jiang-Meka 2023).
